harbor_antrieb_executor.summary:
Implemented Ansible-driven traffic shaping so node2→node3 traffic is capped at 1Mbit/s while node3→node2 stays unrestricted, then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart/recovery protocol on all four managed nodes.

Topology discovered: node1 is a VyOS router (antrieb:vyos:v1) with three NICs — eth0 on the shared management network, eth1 facing node2 (network lan-a), eth2 facing node3 (network lan-b), both dhcp:false and previously unaddressed. node4 is the antrieb:ansible-controller:v1 image and served as the Ansible control node. node2/node3 are RHEL10 hosts.

Work performed from node4 via a single Ansible playbook (/root/site.yml, inventory /root/inventory.ini):
- Enabled passwordless SSH from node4 to node1 (vyos user), node2 (root), node3 (root) using node4's existing keypair.
- On node2: assigned 10.10.12.2/24 to enp8s0 (community.general.nmcli) and added a static route to 10.10.13.0/24 via 10.10.12.1, with a connection down/up cycle since nmcli only pushes new ipv4.routes into the kernel table on reactivation.
- On node3: assigned 10.10.13.2/24 to enp8s0 with a static route to 10.10.12.0/24 via 10.10.13.1, same down/up pattern.
- On node1 (VyOS, via ansible.builtin.raw + the vyos-reference bash -c envelope): addressed eth1 (10.10.12.1/24) and eth2 (10.10.13.1/24), created qos policy shaper LIMIT-TO-NODE3 with `default bandwidth 1mbit`, and attached it as an egress policy on eth2 (the interface node2→node3 traffic transits). Egress-only shaping on eth2 naturally leaves eth1 (node3→node2 egress) unrestricted — no firewall/NAT changes were needed since VyOS forwards by default with no ruleset attached and ip_forward was already 1.
- Verified with iperf3: node2→node3 measured ~1.05 Mbit/s (capped as required); node3→node2 measured ~1.4 Gbit/s (unrestricted). Playbook re-run is idempotent (no config drift on second run).

Mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, interface/route state, service health) on all four nodes, then restarted node4, node2, node3, and finally node1 one at a time using each OS's native mechanism (systemctl reboot for Linux nodes, VyOS `run reboot now`), polling /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id until each node's boot identity changed, and confirming full recovery each time: node4's Ansible tooling and inventory intact and playbook rerunnable; node2/node3's static IPs, routes, and connectivity persisted via NetworkManager; node1's VyOS interface addresses and qos shaper config persisted (confirmed via `show configuration commands`), and the end-to-end 1Mbit/s directional cap was re-verified with iperf3 after node1's restart.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology (interfaces, routes, images) on node1-node4
Set up passwordless SSH from node4 (ansible-controller) to node1 (vyos), node2 (root), node3 (root)
Wrote Ansible inventory (/root/inventory.ini) and playbook (/root/site.yml) on node4
Configured static IPs (10.10.12.0/24, 10.10.13.0/24) and cross routes on node2/enp8s0 and node3/enp8s0 via community.general.nmcli
Configured VyOS node1: addressed eth1/eth2, created qos policy shaper LIMIT-TO-NODE3 (default bandwidth 1mbit), attached as egress policy on eth2 (facing node3)
Verified idempotency by re-running the playbook
Measured throughput with iperf3: node2->node3 ~1.05Mbit/s, node3->node2 ~1.4Gbit/s
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id + health) on all 4 nodes
Restarted node4, node2, node3, node1 one at a time via native reboot mechanisms, polling boot_id for change
Verified post-restart recovery of config/connectivity on each node, and re-verified the directional 1Mbit/s shaping end-to-end after node1's restart
Cleaned up temporary firewalld port openings and iperf3 processes used for testing

evidence.summary: iperf3 from node2 to node3 measured sender 1.05 Mbits/sec sustained over 8s, confirming the cap
iperf3 from node3 to node2 measured ~1.4 Gbits/sec, far above the 1Mbit cap, confirming only one direction is shaped
Playbook/inventory authored on the ansible-controller node4 and executed twice (idempotently) to configure node1 (vyos qos shaper), node2, and node3

evidence.requirement: VyOS config applied via native CLI envelope and persisted (qos policy)
evidence.summary: Confirmed exact qos policy shaper/egress CLI syntax from VyOS templates, applied via bash -c envelope with commit+save, and confirmed it survived a reboot via show configuration commands

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot id, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 416c5cf5..., triggered systemctl reboot, observed disconnect then new boot_id cd6ebb17..., confirmed ansible-playbook still runs cleanly from node4 post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot id, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 19062a82..., triggered systemctl reboot, observed disconnect then new boot_id f1a2e75f..., confirmed IP/route/connectivity to node3 recovered

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot id, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 4ebdfa06..., triggered systemctl reboot, observed disconnect then new boot_id 19983bdc..., confirmed IP/route/connectivity to node2 recovered

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot id, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 4098161f..., triggered VyOS 'reboot now', observed disconnect/reset then new boot_id a11cbcc4..., confirmed interfaces and qos shaper config persisted and re-verified the directional 1Mbit/s cap end-to-end post-restart
